name: Psychometry
description: Psychometry is the alleged paranormal ability to obtain information about an object's history — its past owners, locations, or events surrounding it — by physical contact. The term was coined by American physician Joseph Rodes Buchanan in 1842.
full_description: Psychometry (also called token-object reading or object reading) is a claimed psi modality in which a sensitive holds or touches an object and reports impressions of its history, owners, or associated events. American physician and Eclectic Medical Institute professor Joseph Rodes Buchanan coined the term in 1842, theorising that all things give off persistent emanations that could be 'measured' by trained sensitives; he developed the concept further in his Manual of Psychometry (1893). Geologist William Denton extended the practice into 'geological psychometry' with The Soul of Things (1863), in which his sister and wife reported impressions from rock and fossil specimens. Through the late 19th and early 20th centuries psychometry was a popular feature of Spiritualist seances and stage performances. Selected mediums — notably Stefan Ossowiecki in interwar Poland and Gerard Croiset in the mid-20th-century Netherlands — were tested by parapsychologists and remain reference cases in the field. Modern parapsychology absorbs psychometry-like tasks into broader ESP / clairvoyance protocols. The mainstream scientific consensus is that there is no replicable evidence for psychometry; apparent successes are well explained by cold reading, confirmation bias, and selective reporting. Police agencies overwhelmingly do not consider psychic tipsters useful.
origin: Practised principally in 19th- and 20th-century Anglosphere Spiritualism and 20th-century European parapsychology, though similar 'reading-from-objects' practices appear in many divinatory traditions worldwide.

etymology.origin: Coined in 1842 by Joseph Rodes Buchanan from Greek psychē ('soul, mind') and metron ('measure')
etymology.meaning: Literally 'soul-measuring'; the measurement of an object's psychic 'emanations'
etymology.first_use: Buchanan, J. R. (c.1842); developed in his Manual of Psychometry (1893)

timeline.event: Joseph Rodes Buchanan coins the term 'psychometry' and begins systematic experiments
timeline.significance: Founding moment of the practice as a self-conscious paranormal claim
timeline.source: Buchanan, J. R., Journal of Man (1849–1856); Manual of Psychometry (1893)

timeline.event: Buchanan begins publishing Buchanan's Journal of Man
timeline.significance: Early American Spiritualist / reform venue for psychometry research

timeline.event: William Denton publishes The Soul of Things, extending psychometry to rocks and fossils
timeline.source: Denton, W., & Denton, E. M. F. (1863), The Soul of Things

timeline.event: Buchanan publishes Manual of Psychometry: the Dawn of a New Civilization
timeline.significance: Defining systematic statement of the doctrine

timeline.event: Death of Joseph Rodes Buchanan in San Jose, California
timeline.significance: End of the founder's life; his program continued through Spiritualist popularisers

timeline.event: Stefan Ossowiecki tested by Polish and international parapsychologists, including Charles Richet
W. H. C. Tenhaeff begins systematic testing of Gerard Croiset at Utrecht's parapsychology laboratory
timeline.significance: Mid-20th-century academic testing of object-reading claims

timeline.event: Croiset's death and Tenhaeff scandal: posthumous re-analysis exposes selective reporting
timeline.significance: Major sceptical correction to a well-known psychometry case

related.name: Clairvoyance
related.description: Direct perception of distant or hidden contemporaneous events

related.name: Retrocognition
related.description: Knowledge of past events by anomalous means; psychometry is its object-mediated form

related.name: Remote viewing
related.description: Free-response psi protocol; sometimes uses associated 'targets' analogous to tokens

related.name: Mediumship
related.description: Spiritualist practice in which psychometry was a common feature

related.name: Psychic detective work
related.description: Application of psychometry-like claims to criminal investigations

cultural_notes: Psychometry remains a popular feature of contemporary mediumship and is widely depicted in fiction, despite the absence of replicable scientific evidence.
